We need YOUR help in this final stretch to make sure San Franciscans don’t fall for the lies being spun by the oligarchs and tech elites. Fill out this form and join us ! Bay Get Ready Pledge With election day here, we need to be vigilant and make sure that elections across the country go smoothly without interruption and chaos. But we all know that the Trump administration has already tried to stop the vote through various tactics both here in California, Alaska and other states. As part of the Bay Resistance Coalition, DSA SF is joining in with organizations throughout the Bay Area, including East Bay DSA, to demand that every vote is counted, that all election results are certified without interruption, and that all congressional members are seated on January 3rd, 2027. To that end, we are prepared to join in with our Bay Resistance Coalition partners to stage non-violent, non-cooperation protests throughout the Bay Area if the election is stolen or tampered with. We may have to be on alert all the way through early January. Please sign the attached Bay Resistance voter pledge and receive updates about any actions that will be taking place during this period. The chapter will also send out updates about these actions as well. Sign the Bay Get Ready Pledge Let’s make sure our voices are heard all the way to DC and let the Trump administration know that we will not stand for an authoritarian take over of our elections and country. Home is a Hotel Screening Join us on Saturday, November 7 at 2:00 PM for a film screening of “Home is a Hotel” and a Q&A with Kar Yin Tham, one of the co-directors of the film. Home is a Hotel documents the lives of five single-room occupancy (SRO) residents in San Francisco, the most expensive city in the US, as they fight to keep a roof over their heads and avoid homelessness. SRO residents are often underrepresented when it comes to understanding the material reality of staying housed and homelessness. This event is free, and all are welcome! RSVP here Canvass Workers with SF EWOC The SF local of the Emergency Workplace Organizing Committee (EWOC) wants more workers to be aware of their power and potential for collective organizing! On November 8th at 2:00 PM we’ll be talking to workers on Valencia Street about their hours, pay, and working conditions and encouraging them to unionize with EWOC. The meetup point is 15th and Valencia. No experience necessary! We’ll start with a brief training for everyone. RSVP here EWOC Fundamentals of Workplace Organizing — November Session Do you have problems at your workplace or generally have frustrations with the systems governing your communities? Would you like to learn how to talk to people in order to build collective power? Are you interested in discussing organizing strategies with comrades of various organizing levels? If you said “yes” to any of those questions (or are just a radical person), attend our sessions each Sunday of November 3:00 – 4:30 PM for the EWOC Fundamentals of Workplace Organizing course! Emergency Workplace Organizing Committee (EWOC) is a collaboration between national DSA and the United Electrical, Radio & Machine Workers of America (UE) to organize unorganized workplaces and build a distributed, grassroots organizing program to support workers organizing at the workplace. This training course is meant to help you build your union from the ground up alongside workers in your industry. It doesn’t require an organizing background to understand the material, which covers topics including mapping and charting, building an organizing committee, uniting over common concerns, and how to take action. If you’re interested in becoming any level of organizer for EWOC, this course is mandatory. This course will be in-person, with the group watching the EWOC lectures and the discussion activities occurring at the DSA office (1916 McAllister) . If you can’t make all of the sessions, reach out to san-francisco@workerorganizing.org for accommodations. RSVP here
